key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce electricity costs and improve operation of PV-battery-equipped buildings under dynamic prices, weather, and demand uncertainty.
method: Trained on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for residential energy management.
Used an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, tariffs, weather, calendar/holiday features, and forecasts.
Applied post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned control policies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, with A2C and PPO performing best in cumulative reward and policy stability.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability may depend on data quality, forecasting accuracy, and the ability to generalize across different buildings or operating conditions.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
